title: Readonly Variables and Properties knowledge check

questions.prompt: What does readonly generally guarantee in TypeScript?
options: It recursively freezes all nested values at runtime.
It prevents every other reference from changing the object.
It prevents writes through that typed reference at compile time, but is not by itself runtime immutability.
questions.answer_key: It prevents writes through that typed reference at compile time, but is not by itself runtime immutability.
questions.explanation: Readonly restrictions are type-level contracts unless a separate runtime mechanism enforces immutability.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Readonly Variables and Properties”?
options: A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with readonly properties and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with readonly properties and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “readonly properties”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Readonly Variables and Properties”?
options: Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check readonly arrays and tuples, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume compile-time restrictions versus runtime immutability is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
questions.answer_key: Check readonly arrays and tuples, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Readonly arrays and tuples”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
